title: Which Citation Style Should I Use? 24 Styles | AnswerThis
summary: Compare 24 citation styles and variants by discipline. Check required editions, cite websites, and export references to BibTeX or RIS for review.
body_markdown:
Use the citation style and edition required by your instructor, department, journal or publisher; when none is specified, start with your discipline’s usual system. APA is common in psychology and education, MLA in literary studies, Chicago notes in history, IEEE in engineering and computing, and AMA in medical publishing. Choose the system first, then format verified source details and check them against the publication. AnswerThis’s citation generator helps retrieve and format source records in your selected style, with options to review details, switch styles and export references as BibTeX or RIS.


## **TL;DR**


-


Choose the required citation style before using a citation generator; discipline conventions are a fallback.


-


APA 7 uses author–date citations; MLA 9 usually pairs the author with a passage locator.


-


A website citation identifies the specific page, not just the website homepage.


-


AnswerThis citation pages are free to try for the first 3 sources per browser.


-


BibTeX and RIS carry bibliographic records; inspect imported fields before using the resulting references.


The[AnswerThis citation generator](https://answerthis.io/citation-generator) formats source details for review and export. The IEEE, ACS and Vancouver sections below explain numbered references, their differences and the checks needed before submission.


## Which citation style should I use?


A department can require a style different from its discipline’s common choice. Use one citation system consistently throughout your document.


This table covers **24 selected styles and variants** , not 24 universal standards or the entire generator catalog. Some rows are older editions retained for specific requirements; others are journal or proceedings styles rather than discipline-wide rules.

**A source type is not a citation style.** A website, book or video can be cited in APA, MLA or another system. First identify the work you used; then apply the requested style.


### What is a citation?


A citation is a reference that credits a source and lets readers identify it. Academic documents commonly use a short in-text marker or a note alongside the passage, plus a full reference or bibliography entry. The full entry supplies the relevant author, title, publication details and locator, such as a DOI or URL.


A citation does not establish that a source is reliable or that it supports your claim. Read the original and distinguish its findings from your interpretation.

## Numbered citation styles: IEEE, ACS and Vancouver


IEEE cites sources with square-bracketed numbers assigned in order of first citation and reused for later mentions. Vancouver also numbers sources by first mention, while ACS formatting depends on the journal’s instructions. AnswerThis’s IEEE, ACS and Vancouver generators are free to try for the first 3 sources per browser, shared across citation pages.


A numbered citation style uses a short number in the text to identify a full reference. The number is an address within the manuscript, not a quality score or a publication date. Check both the marker and the full reference because styles differ in punctuation, author treatment and journal abbreviations.


### How to cite in IEEE style


For IEEE citation format, assign a source its number when it first appears and reuse that number whenever you cite the same work. Place the marker in square brackets, such as **\[1\]** , on the text line inside the punctuation. Arrange the reference list by citation order, not alphabetically.


The[IEEE Reference Guide](https://ieeeauthorcenter.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/IEEE-Reference-Guide.pdf) , version dated March 28, 2025, specifies writing cited references out individually rather than compressing a range. Keep the numbering consistent after moving paragraphs or inserting sources. Do not create another bibliography entry merely because you cite a different passage from the same work.


The[AnswerThis IEEE citation generator with numbered references](https://answerthis.io/ieee-citation-generator) uses a pinned CSL style file, meaning a specific saved set of formatting rules. It numbers references using saved-source order, not an automatic reading of your manuscript. Reconcile its numbers with the order of first citation in your final document and reuse existing numbers for repeated sources.


**IEEE example from the generator page:**


```text
[  1  ]    D  .  Kahneman  ,    Thinking  ,    Fast   and   Slow  .  New   York :    Farrar  ,    Straus   and   Giroux  ,    2011.
```


```text
```


```text
```


The IEEE, ACS and Vancouver examples all use the same real book so you can compare formats. The isolated example starts at reference one only because it stands alone. Restore applicable italics in your editor and check the required venue’s instructions before using its punctuation as a template.


### How to cite in ACS style


For ACS citation style, begin with the target chemistry journal’s author guidelines. Do not assume that every ACS publication uses identical markers or reference treatment. The[ACS Guide to Scholarly Communication](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/book/10.1021/acsguide) is the publisher’s guidance resource, while journal-specific instructions determine the submission requirements.


The[AnswerThis ACS citation generator for chemistry papers](https://answerthis.io/acs-citation-generator) selects the standard ACS CSL style. Its worked example uses a numbered reference, but that output does not establish that all chemistry journals request the same treatment. Check chemical notation, technical capitalization and the required journal-name abbreviations against the original source and destination guidance.


**ACS example from the generator page:**


```text
(  1  )    Kahneman  ,    D  .  Thinking  ,    Fast   and   Slow  ;    Farrar  ,    Straus   and   Giroux :    New   York  ,    2011.
```


```text
```


```text
```


The example reproduces the page’s plain-text output, which does not preserve italics or superscript styling. Follow the journal’s requested marker and reference format rather than copying an isolated example without context.


### Vancouver referencing


Vancouver referencing is a numbered system used in biomedical writing. The[ICMJE references guidance](https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/browse/manuscript-preparation/preparing-for-submission.html#g) calls for consecutive numbers in order of first mention and Arabic numerals in parentheses. Use the same assigned number when referring to the publication again.


For full reference formatting, ICMJE points authors to the National Library of Medicine’s[Citing Medicine](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK7256/) . Check journal abbreviations and the target journal’s implementation, since a Vancouver label does not guarantee identical punctuation or electronic-reference treatment everywhere. References first appearing in tables or figure legends also need to follow the manuscript’s citation sequence under ICMJE guidance.


The[AnswerThis Vancouver citation generator for medical journals](https://answerthis.io/vancouver-citation-generator) provides a numbered reference and an in-text example such as **(1)** . Review the saved-source sequence against the manuscript before submission. PubMed metadata helps identify a record but does not by itself settle the required abbreviation or establish that the findings support your statement.


**Vancouver example from the generator page:**


```text
1.    Kahneman   D  .  Thinking  ,    Fast   and   Slow  .  New   York :    Farrar  ,    Straus   and   Giroux  ;    2011.
```


```text
```


```text
```


The plain-text example omits visual styling and cannot demonstrate every source type or journal override. Preserve the verified record and compare the final entry with the required instructions.


### Numbered vs author-date styles


Numbered systems direct the reader to a numbered entry, while author-date systems identify the author and year in the text. Both still require complete source details. The comparison below summarizes how to choose and check the system, not a guarantee that a general preset meets a journal’s rules.


**IEEE**


-


In-text system: Square-bracketed numbers


-


Reference-list organization: Order of first citation


-


Main check: Reuse numbers and follow IEEE and venue guidance


**ACS**


-


In-text system: Depends on the journal’s required treatment


-


Reference-list organization: Follow the selected system and journal instructions


-


Main check: Standard ACS output is not every journal’s format


**Vancouver**


-


In-text system: Numbers, with parentheses under ICMJE guidance


-


Reference-list organization: Order of first mention


-


Main check: Check journal abbreviations and local adaptations


**AMA**


-


In-text system: Superscript numbers


-


Reference-list organization: Citation order


-


Main check: Follow AMA and journal instructions


**APA**


-


In-text system: Author and year


-


Reference-list organization: Alphabetical


-


Main check: Use the required edition and full reference rules


**Harvard**


-


In-text system: Author and year


-


Reference-list organization: Usually alphabetical


-

An ACS reference is not simply an IEEE entry with different brackets, and Vancouver is not a generic substitute for AMA. Changing the visible number without reformatting the full entry leaves a mixed style. If you switch systems, review both the manuscript markers and reference list together.


### What the generators retrieve, and what you still check


All three AnswerThis generators support 12 source types: journal article, book, chapter, website, PDF, image, YouTube video, dataset, thesis, conference paper, software and report. DOIs use Crossref, with DataCite when Crossref has no record, PMIDs use NCBI PubMed, ISBNs use Open Library, and public URLs use the page’s own metadata. **No AI generates citation details, and PDFs are not uploaded or read here.**


The first 3 sources are free per browser, shared across citation pages, not a separate allowance for each style. Editing, changing styles, copying and exporting a saved source do not use another free citation. Users can copy formatted references or export their saved bibliography as BibTeX or RIS.


Retrieved metadata can be incomplete or identify the wrong edition. Check authors, title, source type, date, journal or publisher details and identifiers before formatting. A successful lookup establishes neither that the work is reliable nor that it supports the claim beside the citation, and IEEE, ACS and ICMJE do not endorse these tools.


## How do I cite common sources in APA and MLA?


The[MLA Style Center’s core-element guide](https://style.mla.org/works-cited/works-cited-a-quick-guide/) explains how to assemble an entry from the applicable author, source title, container, contributors, version, number, publisher, date and location. Include only elements that describe the source.


The templates below are copyable field patterns, **not citations to invented publications** . Replace every placeholder with information from the source. An asterisk in a plain-text template marks text that should be italicized in the final reference; remove the asterisks after applying italics in your document.


### How do I cite a website in APA 7?


For a specific webpage, use the author, publication date, page title, site name and URL. If an organization is the credited author, use that organization; do not automatically make the site owner the author. Omit the site name when it is identical to the author. Use **n.d.** when no publication date is available; when no author is credited, move the page title into the author position.


**APA 7 template:**


```text
[  Author   surname ]  ,    [  Initials  ]  .  (  [  Year  ]  ,    [  Month  ]    [  Day  ]  )  . * [  Title   of    page  in    sentence   case  ]  *.  [  Site   name ]  .  [  Page   URL ]
```

```text

```

To build and check your own reference:


1.


Open the exact page you used and record its credited author.


2.


Identify its publication date; do not substitute the footer copyright year.


3.


Record the page title and website name separately.


4.


Format the APA 7 entry, omitting the duplicate site name when appropriate.


5.


Compare the finished entry with the page and add the matching in-text citation.


The website citation generator retrieves public page metadata for review and also accepts manual details. Blocked or incomplete pages require manual checking. APA retrieval dates belong to relevant changing, unarchived content, not automatically to every website citation.


### How do I cite a book in APA and MLA?


Cite the edition you actually read. APA 7 omits the publisher’s location, and an edition other than the first follows the title. Add an available DOI; a print book without a DOI does not need a made-up URL.


```text
APA 7 :    [  Surname  ]  ,    [  Initials  ]  .  (  [  Year  ]  )  . * [  Book   title ]  *  (  [  Edition  ,    if    not   first ]  )  .  [  Publisher  ]  .  [  DOI   or    applicable    URL ]
MLA 9 :    [  Surname  ]  ,    [  First   name ]  . * [  Book   Title ]  *.  [  Edition  ,    if    relevant  ]  ,    [  Publisher  ]  ,    [  Year  ]


```

### How do I cite a journal article in APA and MLA?


Keep the article title separate from the journal title. Check author order, year, volume, issue, pages or article number, and DOI. A DOI is an identifier, not evidence that the findings are valid.


```text

MLA 9 :    [  Surname  ]  ,    [  First   name ]  .  "[Article Title]."   * [  Journal   Name ]  * ,    vol  .  [  Volume  ]  ,    no  .  [  Issue  ]  ,    [  Year  ]  ,    pp  .  [  Page   range ]  .  [  DOI   URL ]


```

### How do I cite a YouTube video?


In APA 7, use the uploader as author, the upload date, italicized video title, **\[Video\]** , YouTube and the URL. When the uploader’s real name and different channel name are known, place the channel name in brackets after the personal name.


```text
APA   7  ,    channel    as   author :
[  Channel   name ]  .  (  [  Year  ]  ,    [  Month  ]    [  Day  ]  )  . * [  Video   title ]  *  [  Video  ]  .  YouTube  .  [  Video   URL ]


APA   7  ,    personal   uploader   plus   different   channel   name :
Surname  ,    A  .  A  .  [  Channel   Name ]  .  (  Year  ,    Month   Day )  . * Title    of   video  *  [  Video  ]  .  YouTube  .  URL


MLA   9  ,    channel   upload :
"[Video Title]."   * YouTube  * ,    uploaded   by    [  Channel   name ]  ,    [  Day  ]    [  Month  ]    [  Year  ]  ,    [  Video   URL ]


```


```text

```



The second APA line is a format pattern, not a named source; retain the brackets around the verified channel name. In MLA, include a relevant identified creator before the title when appropriate, and do not duplicate identical creator and uploader credits.

### How do I cite an image?


Credit the image creator and use the original collection or repository record. A website that displays an image is not necessarily its creator. For an untitled APA image, use a factual bracketed description instead of inventing a title.


```text
APA 7 :
[  Creator   surname ]  ,    [  Initials  ]  .  (  [  Year  ]  )  . * [  Image   title ]  *  [  Photograph  ]  .  [  Collection    or   site   name  ]  .  [  Record   URL ]


APA   7  ,    untitled  - image   format   pattern :
```

## In-text citations, multiple authors and direct quotes


### What is an in-text citation?


An in-text citation is the short marker beside material taken from a source, pointing to its full reference. APA normally uses **(Surname, Year)** ; MLA normally uses **(Surname Page)** when the source has pages. A narrative citation names the author in the sentence; a parenthetical citation puts the relevant details in parentheses.


Numeric systems use numbered markers, but their typography differs: IEEE commonly uses brackets, while AMA uses superscripts. Do not treat bracketed numbers and superscript numbers as interchangeable without checking the required style.


### How do I cite multiple authors in APA?


APA 7 names both authors every time for a two-author work: **(\[Surname\] & \[Surname\], \[Year\])** in parentheses, or **\[Surname\] and \[Surname\] (\[Year\])** in a sentence. For three or more authors, use the first surname and **et al.** from the first citation, unless the shortened forms would be ambiguous.


The reference-list rules are different. APA 7 includes up to **20 authors** . For **21 or more** , list the first **19** , an ellipsis and the final author. Preserve the complete source record rather than shortening its stored author list to match an in-text marker.


MLA 9 names two authors in a two-author citation and uses the first surname plus **et al.** for three or more. Keep any applicable locator.


### How do I cite a direct quote?


Give a locator that lets readers find the exact passage. APA uses a page locator such as **(\[Surname\], \[Year\], p. \[Page\])** ; MLA uses **(\[Surname\] \[Page\])** . If the author is already named in the sentence, avoid repeating information the style does not require.


For an APA webpage without page numbers, use a paragraph number, section heading or a suitable combination. For a video, use the passage timestamp. Do not assign page numbers from a printed webpage or confuse a book’s total length with the page quoted.


APA sets quotations of **40 words or more** as an indented block without quotation marks. MLA uses block format for prose longer than **four lines** ; poetry has separate rules. Both still need a source citation.

## FAQs


### Should I use a discipline’s usual style or my journal’s required edition?


Follow the journal, instructor or department’s explicit requirements first. Discipline conventions are a fallback. Confirm the edition or variant too: a familiar style name does not mean a generator implements the latest manual.


### Can I switch from IEEE to Vancouver by changing the citation brackets?


No. Reformat both the in-text markers and full references, then check citation order, author treatment and journal abbreviations. Reuse each source’s assigned number and follow the destination journal’s instructions.


### Are BibTeX and RIS different citation styles?


No. They store bibliographic records for import into compatible tools; APA, MLA and other styles control their displayed formatting. Check imported fields and do not assume exports transfer PDFs, folders or manuscript citation links.


### Does citing an image give me permission to reproduce it?


No. A reference credits the source, while reproduction rights depend on the license, permission or applicable legal exception. Check the rights statement and any required figure-note attribution separately.


### How does AnswerThis help format and reuse references across styles?


AnswerThis retrieves source metadata or accepts manually checked details, then formats records in your chosen style. You can edit, switch styles, copy or export saved references without another source charge. Verify metadata, the required edition and manuscript numbering before submission.


## Format checked references, then save a reusable copy


Browser-stored references do not automatically move into the app when you sign up. Export a copy before leaving the public generator or converter, then continue working with your sources in AnswerThis if needed.
